title: Business Administrator
description:
We are recruiting a Business Administrator for a client in Leeds. This is a varied and hands-on role that will sit at the heart of the day-to-day operation of the business. The successful candidate will provide support across procurement, supplier management, finance, project administration, logistics and general business operations.

The position would suit somebody who enjoys working in a broad role where no two days are quite the same and who is comfortable coordinating activity across suppliers, projects, finance and internal teams.

Business Administrator - The Role

Working closely with engineering, project and management teams, you will help ensure that purchasing, administration and operational processes run efficiently and accurately.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Managing day-to-day purchasing activities and raising purchase orders.
- Monitoring supplier deliveries, lead times and outstanding orders. Maintaining supplier records and supporting supplier onboarding.
- Liaising with suppliers and expediting orders where required. Supporting supplier performance monitoring and administration.
- Assisting with project procurement planning and tracking project expenditure and purchase commitments.
- Supporting project reporting, schedules and action trackers.
- Assisting with accounts payable, accounts receivable, cashflow forecasting and expenditure tracking.
- Supporting monthly management reporting, budgeting and financial planning activities.
- Providing administrative support for payroll, VAT and other business reporting requirements. Maintaining accurate information within the company's ERP/business management system.
- Processing goods receipts, purchasing transactions and inventory movements. Coordinating incoming and outgoing shipments.
- Preparing shipping and export documentation where required. Supporting stock control, stock takes and inventory accuracy.
- Coordinating the movement of materials between suppliers, customers and company facilities.
- Organising travel, accommodation, meetings and occasional company events.
- Maintaining company records, documentation and filing systems.
- Supporting quality, health & safety and compliance administration.
- Identifying opportunities to improve administrative and operational processes.

Business Administrator - About You

We are looking for an experienced administrator who is comfortable working across several areas of a business and managing multiple priorities.

You are likely to have:
- At least 5 years' experience within business administration, procurement administration, finance administration, project support or a similarly broad operational role.
- Previous experience working within an engineering, manufacturing or technology environment.
- A good understanding of purchasing and supplier management processes.
- Strong organisational and coordination skills.
- Strong Microsoft Office and general IT skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with limited supervision.

Business Administrator - The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to take on a genuinely varied position within an engineering-led organisation, with responsibility spanning procurement, finance, projects, logistics and wider business administration.

The role will suit somebody who enjoys creating structure, keeping operations organised and becoming a trusted point of contact for colleagues, suppliers and other stakeholders.

If you are an experienced Business Administrator looking for a broad role within an engineering or manufacturing environment, we would be interested in hearing from you. Please do apply now!

description:
Job Specification: Load Planner

Department / Location: Transport, Halifax
Reports To: Transport Manager

Main Purpose

To manage day-to-day transport operations, including driver allocation, route planning and transport administration, ensuring customer service requirements are met efficiently and within budget.

Key Responsibilities
- Allocate work to drivers and mates to maximise vehicle utilisation and workforce efficiency, monitoring performance and taking corrective action where necessary.
- Ensure drivers and mates follow company Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and established working practices.
- Plan daily delivery routes using Paragon, ensuring the appropriate vehicles are deployed to meet customer requirements while minimising costs.
- Ensure loads remain within vehicle payload limits and comply with drivers' hours regulations.

- Complete order processing and prepare pick lists, despatch notes and load sheets in accordance with depot procedures.
- Provide support to warehouse management when required.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
- On-time delivery performance.
- Vehicle fill rates and payload utilisation.
- Delivery cost per drop.
- Driver compliance, including drivers' hours and vehicle walk-round checks.
- Completion of training and up-to-date induction records.

Key Working Relationships

Internal
- Transport Manager
- Warehouse Team
- Customer Service Team
- Fleet and Maintenance Team

External
- Customers
- Hauliers and third-party carriers
- Paragon system support

Qualifications, Skills and Experience
- Previous experience in transport planning, ideally using Paragon.
- Working knowledge of drivers' hours regulations and operator licence requirements.
- Strong IT, organisational and communication skills.
- Ability to work under pressure and meet daily delivery deadlines.
- Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to work effectively with drivers, warehouse teams and other departments.
- A proactive approach to improving transport efficiency and customer service.

IT skills are essential, as you will be regularly creating searches, data input and monitoring our achievements and progress against national, local, and internal targets. Key Duties and Responsibilities Patient Reception and Customer Service Act as the first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals, both face-to-face and over the telephone. Welcome patients in a friendly, respectful and professional manner. Respond to general enquiries and provide accurate information about practice services, opening hours and appointment procedures. Deal sensitively with patients who may be anxious, distressed, frustrated or experiencing difficult personal circumstances. Maintain a clean, organised and welcoming reception and waiting area. Manage challenging situations professionally and escalate complaints or concerns to the appropriate member of the practice team. Care Navigation and Appointment Management Handle patient requests for appointments, advice and access to healthcare services by telephone and in person. Use approved care navigation protocols to direct patients to the most appropriate clinician or service, including GPs, practice nurses, clinical pharmacists, physiotherapists and other available services where appropriate. Gather relevant non-clinical information to help determine the appropriate appointment pathway, without attempting to diagnose medical conditions. Book, amend and cancel appointments using the practices clinical computer system. Identify potentially urgent concerns in accordance with practice procedures and promptly escalate them to a clinician. Provide information about alternative services, such as NHS 111, where appropriate and in accordance with practice guidance. Maintain accurate records of patient contacts and appointment requests. Telephone and Administrative Duties Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and manage a busy call queue efficiently. Handle patient messages and ensure they are passed to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice policies and direct medication queries to the appropriate professional. Register new patients and update demographic details, contact information and other relevant records. Manage incoming and outgoing post, emails and electronic communications. Assist with administrative tasks, including recalling patients for appointments, supporting clinical audits and maintaining accurate practice records. Monitor outstanding administrative tasks and follow up requests within agreed timescales. Clinical Systems and Data Management Use the practices electronic clinical system, SystmOne, to access and update patient information. Ensure patient details, appointment information and messages are recorded accurately and promptly. Handle sensitive patient information securely and maintain strict confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, data protection legislation, information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures for accessing, storing and sharing patient information appropriately. Teamwork and Practice Support Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, pharmacists, care coordinators and administrative colleagues. Attend staff meetings and training sessions as required. Support colleagues during busy periods and assist with the day-to-day organisation of reception services. Ongoing training and development will be encouraged to support the delivery of a safe, efficient and high-quality patient service. Personal Qualities We are looking for someone who is approachable, empathetic, dependable and proactive. The successful candidate must demonstrate patience, discretion and professionalism when dealing with sensitive situations and be committed to treating every patient with dignity, respect and fairness. Working Conditions The postholder will work within a busy GP practice and may be required to work flexibly according to the needs of the service. Working hours, salary, annual leave and other employment terms will be confirmed during recruitment.

To welcome patients presenting either in person or by telephone; ensuring you respond promptly and positively. Book appointments for patients and cancel appointments where needed. Support patients in navigating to the most appropriate service, which may include informing patients of external health care providers and online services. Effectively handle all queries that present at the practice; problem solving, signposting and escalation of matters, as appropriate. Ensure patient records are accurate and kept up to date and that all patient contacts are documented in the system using the Care Navigation Template. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare providers. Carrying out administrative duties which include scanning, tasks, out of hours reports, new patient registrations (including basic urine dip), opening and sorting of post (both internal and external), photocopying reports, updating patient details, filing INR reports and data inputting as requested. Processing medication requests, including issuing repeat medication and appliance items, as well as forwarding patient requests onto the practice pharmacy team/on-call GP. Communicating effectively with local pharmacy staff and resolving/investigating any queries they may have. Processing e-consults via system one and triaging the patient accordingly using signposting where necessary. Opening up/locking up of practice premises and maintaining security in accordance with practice protocols. Carry out chronic disease recalls and vaccination campaigns, booking relevant appointments working from a list to ensure clinics are fully utilised Informing patients of test results and following up with instructions from clinicians. Keeping the reception area and notice boards clean, tidy and up to date. Taking payments for private documents from patients and providing receipts Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required. Assisting the Site Co-ordinator with weekly fire alarm checks and weekly/monthly legionella testing, when required. Assisting the Site Co-ordinator with weekly room plans and petty cash records, when required. To be able to work with people from a wide variety of cultures and backgrounds, and people with disabilities and learning difficulties, and to be able to communicate with them (and, when necessary, their carers) appropriately to facilitate their care and understanding of their care within the service. Attend and positively contribute to team meetings. Fully comply with all company Health and Safety requirements, including reporting all accidents, near accidents, and hazards. Treat all patients fairly and with respect. Provide cover across all sites as required. This is not an exhaustive list, and it is expected that this role will develop as the business grows.

title: Clinical Administrator

You will play a vital role in supporting clinicians within a busy service, helping ensure patients receive a professional, responsive and positive experience throughout their care journey. We're looking for someone who: Puts people first providing caring, professional and compassionate customer service to patients, colleagues and visitors. Thrives in a busy environment staying organised, prioritising tasks and supporting the smooth running of the service. Takes a proactive approach using initiative, embracing a can-do attitude and finding practical solutions. Works as part of a team communicating effectively and working flexibly to meet the needs of the service. title: Care Navigator/Receptionist
description: Due to a member of the team upskilling into a new role, we are seeking a Care Navigator/Receptionist to join our fast-paced reception and administration team. We are looking for individuals who feel they will be able to settle into a busy practice, whilst able to work independently and as part of a team. Previous primary care or GP surgery experience is desirable, although applicants with relevant transferable skills will also be considered. Provide a professional and welcoming first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. Manage a busy telephone system, responding to enquiries and directing patients to the most appropriate service. Book, amend and cancel patient appointments in accordance with practice protocols. Receive patients at the reception desk, recording arrivals and assisting with enquiries. Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures. Deal with incoming emails, post and other administrative correspondence. Liaise effectively with GPs, nurses, pharmacists, hospitals and other healthcare organisations. Carry out administrative tasks relating to patient records, including scanning, document management and filing. Follow practice protocols to ensure consistent and high-quality care is provided to our patients. Act as directed by other members of the practice team. Provide reception and administrative cover for colleagues during periods of annual leave or sickness absence. Work across both Ireland Wood and Horsforth practice sites when required. Ensure confidentiality is always maintained in accordance with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and practice policies. The Care Navigator/Receptionist is an essential member of the practice team, providing a professional, efficient and patient-focused reception and administrative service across both practice sites. Working closely with the Practice Manager, GP Partners and the wider clinical and administrative teams, the post-holder will help ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the practice while delivering excellent customer service to patients and visitors. A key part of the role is supporting patients with their queries and appointment requests, helping them to access the most appropriate healthcare professional or service in line with practice protocols. The post-holder will manage appointments, respond to telephone and face-to-face enquiries, process repeat prescription requests and undertake a range of administrative duties to support the delivery of safe and effective patient care. The role also includes maintaining accurate patient records, processing correspondence and supporting communication with hospitals, pharmacies and other healthcare organisations. The post-holder will work in accordance with practice policies, maintain confidentiality at all times, and provide cover for colleagues and across both practice sites when required. Overall, this is a varied and rewarding role that requires excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, together with the ability to work calmly and effectively in a busy environment while providing a high standard of patient care and customer service.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Stanley Health Centre is looking for an enthusiastic, flexible and reliable receptionist to join our Reception team. Successful candidates will need to be able to demonstrate previous administrative and customer service experience and have the skills to adapt to and prioritise the duties of a busy reception desk, remaining calm and focused to ensure a high standard of care is delivered to patients. The ideal candidate will be a team player with excellent verbal and written communication skills. Computer skills are essential, and experience with a clinical system would be advantageous, but training will be provided for the right candidate. The post holder will also need to be flexible in their hours to cover either mornings or afternoons when required, working part-time 25 hours per week either 8am to 1pm or 1.30pm 6.30pm Monday to Friday. Stanley Health Centre Receptionist job description Job Title: Medical Receptionist Line Manager: Assistant Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Manager Hours per week: 25 To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of information and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. Mission Statement We will strive to: Provide a service which puts patients needs and welfare at the heart of everything we do. Generic Responsibilities All staff at Stanley Health Centre have a duty to conform to the following: Equality, Diversity & Inclusion A good attitude and positive action towards ED&I creates and environment where all individuals are able to achieve their full potential. Creating such an environment is important for three reasons: it improves operational effectiveness, it is morally the right thing to do, and it is required by law. Patients and their families have the right to be treated fairly and be routinely involved in decisions about their treatment and care. They can expect to be treated with dignity and respect and will not be discriminated against on any grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Patients have a responsibility to treat other patients and our staff with dignity and respect. Staff have the right to be treated fairly in recruitment and career progression. Staff can expect to work in an environment where diversity is valued and equality of opportunity is promoted. Staff will not be discriminated against on any grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Staff have a responsibility to ensure that you treat our patients and their colleagues with dignity and respect. Safety, Health, Environment and Fire (SHEF) This practice is committed to supporting and promoting opportunities to for staff to maintain their health, well-being and safety. You have a duty to take reasonable care of health and safety at work for you, your team and others, and to cooperate with employers to ensure compliance with health and safety requirements. All personnel are to comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, Environmental Protection Act 1990, Environment Act 1995, Fire Precautions (workplace) Regulations 1999 and other statutory legislation. Confidentiality This practice is committed to maintaining an outstanding confidential service. Patients entrust and permit us to collect and retain sensitive information relating to their health and other matters, pertaining to their care. They do so in confidence and have a right to expect all staff will respect their privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. It is essential that if, the legal requirements are to be met and the trust of our patients is to be retained that all staff protect patient information and provide a confidential service. Quality & Continuous Improvement (CI) To preserve and improve the quality of our output, all personnel are required to think not only of what they do, but how they achieve it. By continually re-examining our processes, we will be able to develop and improve the overall effectiveness of the way we work. The responsibility for this rests with everyone working within the practice to look for opportunities to improve quality and share good practice. This practice continually strives to improve work processes which deliver health care with improved results across all areas of our service provision. We promote a culture of continuous improvement, where everyone counts and staff are permitted to make suggestions and contributions to improve our service delivery and enhance patient care. Induction Training On arrival at the practice all personnel are to complete a practice induction programme; this is managed by the Deputy Practice Manager. Learning and Development The effective use of training and development is fundamental in ensuring that all staff are equipped with the appropriate skills, knowledge, attitude and competences to perform their role. All staff will be required to partake and complete mandatory training as directed by the training coordinator, as well as participating in the practice training programme. Staff will also be permitted (subject to approval) to undertake external training courses which will enhance their knowledge and skills, progress their career and ultimately, enable them to improve processes and service delivery. Collaborative Working All staff are to recognise the significance of collaborative working. Teamwork is essential in multidisciplinary environments. Effective communication is essential and all staff must ensure they communicate in a manner which enables the sharing of information in an appropriate manner. Service Delivery Staff at Stanley Health Centre must adhere to the information contained with practice policies and regional directives, ensuring protocols are adhered to at all times. Staff will be given detailed information during the induction process regarding policy and procedure. Security The security of the practice is the responsibility of all personnel. Staff must ensure they remain vigilant at all times and report any suspicious activity immediately to their line manager. Under no circumstances are staff to share the codes for the door locks to anyone and are to ensure that restricted areas remain effectively secured. Professional Conduct Practice staff are required to dress appropriately for their role. Administrative staff will be provided with a uniform whilst clinical staff must dress in accordance with their role. Leave All personnel are entitled to take leave. Line managers are to ensure all of their staff are afforded the opportunity to take their allocated amount of annual leave each year, and should be encouraged to take all of their leave entitlement.

title: MEDICAL RECEPTIONIST
description: We need a reliable, motivated, hard working and flexible individual to join our friendly busy team. Must have SystmOne experience withgood computer and communication skills. To work 25.5 hours per week To commence as soon as possible. FLEXIBILITY IS ESSENTIAL TO THIS ROLE. Greeting and directing patients and visitors on arrival. Signposting patients to the most appropriate healthcare professional. Registering new patients. Booking appointments. Using photocopier, telephone, email and clinical system. Respond to the needs of clinicians during surgery. Respond to requests from Management. Preparing consultation rooms, prior to and after surgery. General housekeeping (e.g. keeping waiting and office areas clean and tidy). Action tasks on SystmOne Provide clerical assistance to support the delivery of patient services, e.g. post, data input and scanning. Specified Duties To provide and effective, polite and efficient point of contact to all patients and visitors to the Practice. To create and instil an atmosphere of calm, pleasant and peaceful surrounds. Maintain a positive attitude at all times. Smile when you answer the phone. Remember never say it is not my job to. Always say what you can do, not what you cannot do. Acknowledge and welcome the arrival of patients with a booked appointment at the front desk. Make future appointments and allocate appropriate same day appointments. Liaise with duty doctor via SystmOne any instructions regarding the processing of lists that are undertaken in line with the agreed procedure. Answer the telephone within 4 rings and ensure all messages are recorded in SystmOne and are dealt with or passed to the appropriate person for action. Deal with actions arising from the post when dealt with by the duty doctor. Deal with prescriptions requests and home visit requests as they come in, on the telephone and face to face. Make up a visit list each day and print out a patient summary relating to each person being visited. Exhibit willingness to train on new technology and updated systems, as required. Ensure all aspects of Health and safety are adhered to and breaches reported to Management. Flexibility when asked to cover shifts for holidays, sickness, absences remember you never know when you might need cover. Generally keeping the reception area, in fact all areas clean and tidy. Scan all post into SystmOne record as agreed. Ensure accurate data entry onto SystmOne according to protocols. Liaise with other Health Care professionals, as and when necessary to ensure relevant people are advised of developments, which affect patients under their care. To work in a manner that ensures the smooth running of the Practice. Receiving and receipting monies. Using email facilities as an internal communication tool. At the end of the day ensure all areas of reception are tidy in order to ensure easy accessibility for the cleaners. To ensure all areas are secure at night, all electrical equipment is switched off and that the building is secure when last to leave. Ensure phone lines are switched over to the preferred out of hours provider. Complete all tasks relevant to position. Complete and maintain targets as set out and agreed by the Practice Manager in annual appraisal. Read and adhere to all protocols. Work as a team Filing with accuracy Use alert/reminder templates Prescriptions pull out non-collected ones after 3 months Change patient names and addresses Stocking up clinical rooms Maintain security of the premises Maintain ultimate confidentiality This job description is not exhaustive and therefore other duties may be asked of you by the clinic/management team if within your physical and educational capabilities.
